messages.author: 976377e9257b5df0
messages.subject: Issue with recordTable() reading video files
parts:
Hi Juergen,

I am in the process of using a small sample of video files to learn camtrapR and get the workflow figured out before using it for a large dataset. I am using Digikam and have the database file located in within a 'session' folder containing the station subdirectories (attached).

I ran into some issues with recordTable(), where I received the following error message for station folders that contain videos,

Warning:  090.1.2:   metadataSpeciesTag 'Species' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'.

I have been troubleshooting this problem with Joel Ruprecht, who has experience with using video files in camtrapR, and here's what we've figured out.

-If a photo (jpg file) is copied into any of the station folders, recordTable() is able to read it correctly with all of it associated tags, although it cannot read the video files. This is when I have InDir set to the same file path as the attached snip, 'digikam_db_location(2)'.

-If InDir is changed to a particular station folder (e.g. ".../W20/069.7.1"), recordTable() can read all of those video files correctly along with all of their associated tags.

-Using the source code (attached) confirmed that the tag info is being correctly read from the database.

Any ideas as to whether or not this is an issue on my end? Also, I realize that before I include data from a new session, I will need to move the digikam database files to the folder containing the different sessions (e.g. W20, W21, etc.). Not sure how relevant that is, but I wanted to clarify that my database files and video files will have to be separated by several folders.

Thanks very much for the help with this!

Wes

messages.author: bba8ce58a28a6363
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Issue with recordTable() reading video files
parts:
Hi Juergen,

I just wanted to provide a few details about my experience having similar issues with a different dataset. When I called recordTable() to extract tags from videos with inDir set to the folder containing all the stations, it worked perfectly for 25 out of 28 stations. But for 3 stations, I got the same warning message "metadataSpeciesTag 'Species' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'" even though those 3 stations had 'Species' video tags. When I then pointed inDir to the station folder for each of those 3 stations, it extracted the video tags fine. I can find no pattern to the 3 problematic stations (e.g. it happened on 2 camera types, Browning and Bushnell, and two file types, mp4 and avi).

For me it wasn't a big deal, I just ran recordTable() on the 3 stations separately and used rbind() to combine them. So although my issue is resolved, I just wanted to provide these details in case it helps with troubleshooting for others with larger datasets.

Thanks for all your work on this fine package!

Joel

Hi Raquel,
the metadata of this file have no "QuickTime:CreateDate" tag, therefore the recordTable code you shared can't extract any date/times from the video files. There's not much we can do if the date-time tag is missing. That's due to the manufacturer of the cameras. 

Is FileModifyDate correct by any chance? That can potentially be used, but that is usually a bad choice because it can be overwritten automatically very easily when editing files, so it is not robust. Even if FileModifyDate should be correct, you'd need to run recordTable separately to extract the data for the avi files (you can't use QuickTime:CreateDate and FileModifyDate at the same time for the video(dateTimeTag ...) argument).

Even if the date-time in that tag is not correct, you might at least be able to get a table in which you'd afterwards need to change the date/time (manually if need be).

Or, one last idea, if you can convert the video to a jpg (e.g. the first frame), you might be able to use the new functions OCRdataFields and writeDateTimeOriginal to extract the date/time in the data field of the video and write it into the jpg representing the video. Not ideal, but it may save you the hassle of modifying date/time tags manually in the recordTable. These two functions are only available in the github version (pre-release).

library(remotes) 
install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR")

Best,
Jürgen

El lun, 5 de abr. de 2021 a la(s) 10:27, Juergen Niedballa (camt...@gmail.com) escribió:

Hi Raquel,
the metadata of this file have no "QuickTime:CreateDate" tag, therefore the recordTable code you shared can't extract any date/times from the video files. There's not much we can do if the date-time tag is missing. That's due to the manufacturer of the cameras. 

Is FileModifyDate correct by any chance? That can potentially be used, but that is usually a bad choice because it can be overwritten automatically very easily when editing files, so it is not robust. Even if FileModifyDate should be correct, you'd need to run recordTable separately to extract the data for the avi files (you can't use QuickTime:CreateDate and FileModifyDate at the same time for the video(dateTimeTag ...) argument).

Even if the date-time in that tag is not correct, you might at least be able to get a table in which you'd afterwards need to change the date/time (manually if need be).

Or, one last idea, if you can convert the video to a jpg (e.g. the first frame), you might be able to use the new functions OCRdataFields and writeDateTimeOriginal to extract the date/time in the data field of the video and write it into the jpg representing the video. Not ideal, but it may save you the hassle of modifying date/time tags manually in the recordTable. These two functions are only available in the github version (pre-release).

library(remotes) 
install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR")

Best,
Jürgen

Hi, 
exifTagNames() expects the images / video to be in station directories within inDir. Above there was no subdirectory to ..."ALCIDES", and the function said: "File not found". 

In this case it might be better to specify exactly which file you wish to analyze with the fileName argument, e.g. 

exifTagNames(fileName = "E:/DATOS_TESIS/REV_CAM_Junio-Julio19/ALCIDES/IMG_0001.AVI")

Feel free to share the output of that. For recordTable, the argument "video" has to be set according to what you find in the exif data of the videos. That's the next step. 

Best regards,
Jürgen
